content: Rhodamine B is a fluorescent dye commonly utilized in biological applications as a staining agent. It is often employed in conjunction with Auramine O to create the auramine-rhodamine stain, which is specifically used to identify acid-fast organisms, such as Mycobacterium species. When used as a laser dye, Rhodamine B exhibits tunable fluorescence around a wavelength of 610 nm. In the state of California, Rhodamine B is classified as a suspected carcinogen. Consequently, any products containing this compound are required to display a warning label to inform users of its potential carcinogenic risks.
